summary: Iteration 5 backend security batch — 26/26 tests passed in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration5.py. Validated: password strength (8+ chars, digit, special), 18+ DOB hard block with minor_block_attempts logging + no user creation, JWT exp ~30 days, bcrypt $2b$12$ hash, Fernet message encryption at rest (DB content starts 'gAAAA', plaintext NOT in DB, decrypted on GET), 2FA toggle/login challenge/verify with replay+wrong+expired = 401, account deletion request (pending_deletion_at +30d)/cancel/confirm cascade delete with 'DELETE FOREVER' guard, CCPA ZIP export contains 7 expected files (no password leak), Private Mode 402 for free + 200 for VIP, enhanced /api/safety/block deletes matches+messages+swipes, admin /api/admin/security/flags 403 non-admin + suspend/unsuspend/dismiss actions work, security headers present (X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, HSTS), suspicious detection (messaging_spam high → auto-suspend, swipe_bot_behavior high), rate limits 5/min register & 10/min login. Discover regression OK.

minor.issue: Age computed as days // 365 — leap years can off-by-one a user exactly on their 18th birthday. Use relativedelta or proper year math for production accuracy.
After enabling 2FA, existing JWT tokens issued BEFORE the toggle remain valid indefinitely (no session revocation). Enabling 2FA should ideally invalidate prior tokens.

Cascade deletes from sender_id only — messages SENT by other party in deleted user's matches remain orphaned with match_id pointing to a deleted match. Consider deleting by match_id of the user's matches as well.

send_email asyncio.create_task is never awaited and the task is destroyed when the request handler returns — visible as 'Task was destroyed but it is pending' warnings on shutdown. Tasks should be tracked or awaited.

Server comment says 'AES-128 via Fernet' but Fernet uses AES-128-CBC — spec called for AES-256. Fernet's 128-bit cipher is fine for production but doesn't match the AES-256 wording in the spec. Either update the spec/comment or migrate to AESGCM-256.
slowapi in-memory limiter is per-process; with multiple worker processes (gunicorn) the effective limit would be 5*N register/min. Production should use Redis backend.

Not strictly an issue — but get_remote_address behind a proxy/Cloudflare returns the proxy IP. All users on the same edge share the same rate-limit bucket. Should respect X-Forwarded-For via slowapi's forwarded_address.

action_items: Comment in server.py line 256 says 'AES-128 via Fernet' but earlier iterations referred to AES-256 — clarify in spec/docs (Fernet uses AES-128-CBC under the hood; this is industry-standard but technically not AES-256).
Track or await fire-and-forget asyncio.create_task(send_email(...)) tasks to silence 'Task was destroyed but it is pending' warnings during pytest shutdown.
Consider session invalidation when /api/auth/2fa/toggle is flipped on (rotate JWT or bump a session-version field).
Use relativedelta (python-dateutil) instead of (days//365) for the 18+ age computation to avoid leap-year off-by-one.
Cascade delete on /api/account/delete/confirm could also remove inbound messages (any message in deleted user's matches), not just sender_id rows.
Production: move slowapi to a Redis backend so rate limits are shared across worker processes & honor X-Forwarded-For.
server.py is now 2044 lines — overdue for split (auth, safety/admin-security, account-deletion, messaging routers).
critical_code_review_comments: encrypt_str / decrypt_str gracefully handle legacy plaintext on decrypt (returns cipher unchanged on InvalidToken) — good for forward-compat.
send_message uses encrypt_str(msg.content); voice messages remain unencrypted (content holds URL). Spec ambiguous — confirm intent.
validate_password_strength regex includes special chars but no upper-case requirement — spec only asked digit+special, so this is correct; mentioning for visibility.
/api/admin/security/resolve does NOT validate action is one of dismiss|suspend|unsuspend — an unknown action just resolves the flag without side effects. Add an enum check.
/api/account/delete/confirm cascades delete on db.messages by sender_id — leaves orphaned recipient messages. Combined with match deletion this is mostly fine but technically inconsistent.

minor_block_attempts stores email_hash as bcrypt(email)[:60] — bcrypt has internal salt so the same email hashes differently every call; this defeats the purpose of de-duping minor signups by hashed email. Use sha256 if dedup is desired.
Suspicious-messaging window query uses ISO string lexical compare ($gte: one_hour_ago.isoformat()) — works only because timestamps are tz-aware ISO with consistent format; add an index hint.
JWT_SECRET defaults to a hardcoded string if env var missing — fine for dev but should fail-fast in production.
